newsitem.title: USA: AOL unit to buy Lightspeed, form network.
newsitem.headline: AOL unit to buy Lightspeed, form network.

text.p: America Online Inc's Greenhouse Networks division said Monday it was acquiring LightSpeed Media, a pioneer producer of Internet soap operas and shows.
Greenhouse also said former NBC executive Brandon Tartikoff had been named chairman of the Greenhouse board.

Terms of the LightSpeed deal were not disclosed. But as part of the deal, Greenhouse, which is AOL's original content division, said it would develop an interactive entertainment network, scheduled for launch this autumn.
Tartikoff will continue to head up his own production company and act as a consultant and adviser to AOL as chairman of Greenhouse.

LightSpeed was the creator of the first so-called "episodic" show on the Internet, called "The Spot," which it sold to American Cybercast in early 1996. "The Spot," a soap opera about five California housemates, is still on the Web site of AMCY, which filed for Chapter 11 in January.
LightSpeed was founded in May 1996 by the creators of "The Spot." Founder Scott Zakarin will be named president of programming.
Zakarin and his team launched another episodic Internet show, called "GrapeJam," in August 1996.

AOL executives say Internet soap operas will be only a small part of its entertainment network, which will feature celebrity hosts, real-time events, news and other information about the entertainment industry.
"The focus is on the entertainment industry and the entertainment business," said Danny Krifcher, president and CEO of Greenhouse.
He declined to say how big the venture will be.

AOL plans to make money from the entertainment network through advertising revenues, licensing, and through transcations, such as selling tickets to entertainment events, selling merchanside, and offering premium information at a surcharge. Krifcher declined to make any revenue or profit forecasts.
The network's closest competition on the Internet are sites such as Mr. Showbiz, E! Online and a People magazine site devoted to entertainment, AOL said.
"This is the beginning of what we think will be a series of exciting announcements and developments for us," Krifcher said.
